name: Adaptive Fluid Sampling (Splitting and Merging)
definition: A technique to improve simulation accuracy and visualization in geometrically complex regions by splitting particles, and to improve computational efficiency by merging nearby particles deep inside the fluid.
summary: Adaptive Fluid Sampling dynamically adjusts SPH particle density by splitting surface particles and merging inner ones, differing from static methods by using local geometry to balance visual fidelity and computational cost.
